title: Bhishma's fall
hook: two kinds of arrows reach Bhishma, and he can tell them apart

segments.voice: Your line was Bhishma's fall, and yesterday we went back a lifetime, to Amba, the princess who would be born again as Shikhandi. Whose older story did you notice? Day eight hundred twenty-nine.

Two kinds of arrows are flying at Bhishma's chariot. Some come from Shikhandi, standing in front, exactly as Bhishma himself advised. Bhishma doesn't answer them. He keeps his bow lowered toward that one warrior, the way he said he would. And behind Shikhandi, using him as cover, Arjuna is shooting too. Bhishma has trained and fought beside these archers for a lifetime. Today, the moment he stops guessing whose arrows are reaching him.

In Ganguli's English, Bhishma speaks as the arrows pierce him. These aren't Shikhandi's, he says, in effect. They cut too deep. These are Arjuna's. He names his grandson's arrows as they strike him, and he still doesn't turn his weapons on Shikhandi. Then he falls from his chariot. And here the epic gives a picture all its own. So many arrows are lodged in his body that he never touches the ground. He lies on them, held above the earth, on a bed of arrows. The fighting stops. Warriors on both sides drop their weapons and stand still. The Kauravas and the Pandavas, who were killing each other a moment ago, gather around the same old man. And Bhishma doesn't die. Long ago, the text says, his father granted him a gift for his vow: he would die only when he chose to. Lying there, he sees that the sun is moving in its southern course, and he decides it's not yet the time. He'll wait for the sun to turn north. The epic adds one more detail. Sages come to him in the form of swans, sent from his mother, the river goddess Ganga, and remind him of the sun's course, and he answers that he'll hold on. Bhishma's fall isn't a single crash. It's a man brought down by the truth he told, lying still on the field, choosing his own hour.
screen: `THESE ARE ARJUNA'S ARROWS` · `HE NEVER TOUCHES THE GROUND` · `BOTH ARMIES STAND STILL` · then, large: `HE CHOOSES HIS HOUR`

segments.voice: Lie down if you can, or sit back and let the chair hold your whole weight. Notice every place your body is supported: your back, your legs, your head. Breathe in, and let yourself be held. Breathe out, and let the noise around you go still, the way both armies went still around Bhishma. Nothing to fight for these two minutes. If you pray, you can rest in prayer, held. The bell holds the time.
Bhishma's fall. The grandsire on a bed of arrows, held above the ground, waiting for the sun to turn.
Your line: Bhishma's fall. Today, when a fight around you stops for a moment, don't rush to restart it. Let the stillness stand. Day eight hundred twenty-nine.

howItsDone: The image of Bhishma on his bed of arrows, in Sanskrit shara-shayya, appears in temple art, paintings and retellings of the epic.

myth: Bhishma fought back hard against Shikhandi at the end
he kept his weapons from Shikhandi, as he had said he would.
when Bhishma fell, his body never touched the ground
the arrows held him up: a bed of arrows.
Bhishma died the moment he fell
his father's gift let him choose his hour, and he chose to wait for the sun to turn north.

fork.setup: you're Bhishma, lying on the arrows, and the gift of choosing your hour is yours. the sun is in its southern course. what do you do?
options: let go now, while the battle still rages.
wait for the sun to turn north.
ask to be carried home to Hastinapura.
fork.reveal: he holds on, and the swans sent by Ganga find him still waiting for the sun's northern turn.

original.note: bed of arrows: the name for Bhishma's resting place on the field.

trapdoor: what you thought: Bhishma was killed in battle.
what it means: he was brought down, but by his father's gift he chose when he would die.
what a scholar hears: the waiting turns the fall into a deathbed, and the field of war into a place where he will teach before he goes.

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli that Bhishma distinguishes Arjuna's arrows from Shikhandi's as they strike, and that his body does not touch the ground.
Confirm the swans are sages (rishis) sent by Ganga and that they speak of the sun's southern course; confirm both armies lay down weapons around him.
howItsDone mentions Bhishma Ashtami in Magha only generally; a Keeper may name it or cut it.
Original word शरशय्या: confirm Devanagari form; the teach uses 'bed of arrows' without the Sanskrit to avoid an unchecked etymology on the voice track.

Editor: cut stock phrasing ('strange, unforgettable pictures', 'quiet, luminous detail') and the claim that he knows 'every bow on that field'; howItsDone no longer mentions a Magha observance the cited text doesn't give.
The trapdoor's third floor anticipates Bhishma's later teaching (Shanti and Anushasana Parvas); confirm the serial covers it.
